title: Cross-Org OKR Flightplan and Initiative Staging Guidance
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Overview:
This ticket captures a prescriptive playbook for sequencing and staging company-level OKRs and associated initiatives across product, engineering, design, and GTM. The goal is to reduce ambiguity in quarterly handoffs, create clear staging gates for cross-functional dependencies, and provide a lightweight operational cadence that teams can adopt without heavy process overhead.

Problem statement:
We repeatedly see initiative drift after OKRs are set: teams misalign on critical dependencies, rollout windows collide, and downstream work (Docs, Console UX, Dedicated/Self-host rollout) is surfaced late. This causes scope churn, missed SLAs for Dedicated customers, and overstretched infra during spikes.

Goals (success criteria):
- A repeatable staging model that reduces cross-team blockers by 40% in Q1 2026 (measured via dependency resolution time).
- Clear ownership and gating criteria for major initiatives so at-risk work is identified two cycles earlier.
- Minimum viable artifact set produced at each gate: PRD snapshot, rollout checklist, cost/latency impact estimate, monitoring deck.

Proposal (high level):
1) Introduce a 3-stage "flightplan" for every company-level initiative: Scoped → Validated → Staged.
   - Scoped: PM and Eng agree on outcomes, KPIs, rough sequencing, and dependency map.
   - Validated: engineering spike and design prototype validated; initial rollout plan and metrics defined; security/compliance check queued.
   - Staged: full release checklist completed, canary plan and rollback defined, customer comms drafted.
2) Gate definitions and artifacts (templates linked below). Each gate requires sign-off from PM, Eng Lead, and Design Lead. Security/compliance sign-off required before Staged if sensitive.
3) A lightweight dependency registry (spreadsheet + Confluence view) where teams declare blocking resources and estimated resolution dates. RBAC limited to initiative leads to avoid noise.
4) Monthly cross-functional staging review (30–45 minutes) where active initiatives present status against gates; follow-ups issued as action items.

Artifacts and templates (examples):
- Scoped template (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinc.com/pages/Scoped-Template
- Release checklist (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/release-checklists-2026
- Dependency registry (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/dep-registry-2026

Decision log / trade-offs:
- We debated a heavier gating board (full JIRA workflow) vs. lightweight staging spreadsheet. Chosen: spreadsheet + Confluence because adoption speed is critical and we want low friction for teams that ship rapidly (Decision 2025-11-12).
- Opted not to require full security review at Validated stage to avoid blocking early validation; instead security enters a queued review and is required before Staged when customer-facing or handling PII (Trade-off: slightly higher security coordination risk vs. faster product validation).

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook published to Confluence and linked from the company roadmap page.
- Templates created for Scoped/Validated/Staged artifacts and accessible to all teams.
- Pilot run with 3 initiatives (one each from Runtime, Console, and Dedicated) completed by end of Q1 cycle and retrospective produced.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Publish playbook and templates; announce at company all-hands.
- Weeks 1–4: Pilot with 3 initiatives (Runtime: batching improvements; Console: rollout UX; Dedicated: autoscaler controls).
- Week 5: Collect feedback and iterate templates.
- Week 6: Enable registry and schedule recurring monthly staging review.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Dependency resolution time (days) per initiative (baseline and target).
- % of initiatives meeting the Staged gate on or before planned release week.
- Number of cross-team blockers raised in last 6 weeks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Low adoption due to perceived process overhead. Mitigation: keep templates minimal; productize the registry view in Confluence; run office hours for first 6 weeks.
- Risk: Gate sign-offs delay work. Mitigation: enforce SLAs for reviewers (48–72 hours) and allow PM-escrow sign-off for critical paths.

Next steps:
- Draft Confluence playbook and templates (owner: Maya Chen) — due 2025-11-18.
- Schedule pilot champions (Runtime: Diego Morales, Console: Asha Patel, Dedicated: Rahul Singh).
- Configure dependency sheet and populate with pilot initiatives.

Related links:

- Pilot initiative tracker (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/pilot-initiatives-2026
- Example PRD snapshot (Drive): https://drive.google.com/file/d/example-prd.pdf
